# CoreWeave

## F3Q Review: Margin Inflection Ahead of Plan and Progress Towards Self-
Funding Address Key Investor Debates; Reiterate OW

  
---  
  
By Samik Chatterjee, CFA
AC,
Jaiden R
Patel,
Noah R
Herman,
Mashu
Nishi

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
CRWV, CRWV US  
Price (10 Nov 26):$48.73  
Price Target (Dec-27):$125.00  
  
CoreWeave’s 3Q results and commentary should address concerns that investors
have about reliance on access to capital markets, with the company laying out
a robust plan towards its ability to address committed backlog in 2027 with
less than $5B of parent level equity (or equity linked) raises, and the
improvement in the industry fundamentals including compressed payback periods
on short-term contracts driving the company to increasingly move towards self-
funding. Key stand-outs that investors concerned about the economics of
contracts as well as the incremental capital needs to fund capex should note:
1) Operating margins in 3Q26 reached low double-digits (10%), a quarter ahead
of plan; the company guided 4Q26 to ~16% operating margins highlighting that
the recent favorable economics are rapidly helping the company towards the
long-term margin outlooks it has outlined in the past; 2) Prepayments from
customers are already ramping (including for renewal contracts), which in
conjunction with OEM financing, will support a cash flow burn that is more
modest than previously anticipated; 3) Capital cost of asset-back debt has not
moved in sync with cost of unsecured debt, contrary to investor fears, and the
company outlined that it is confident in getting new DDTL deals done
relatively soon; 4) the company sees no need for any unsecured debt raises in
calendar 2027; and 5) the company can bridge the gap between its capex plans
and DDTL debt (undrawn capacity and new deals), prepayments, OEM financing and
operating cash flow generated from existing capacity through less than $5B of
parent level capital, much more modest than investor perception heading into
the print. While on the earnings call, the company laid out a scenario of
capex tracking flat y/y in 2027 were it to focus only on addressing the
committed backlog; we want to clarify that the company is not guiding to
curtailing growth in capacity and instead only outlining a scenario to address
investor concerns around the magnitude of capital raises; on top of the
former, we expect the company to be able to fund growth in capex and capacity
and still remain within the guardrails of the less than $5B of parent level
capital raise outlined for 2027. The results and outlined plans further
amplify our confidence in the health of the fundamental drivers of the
business, even before considering the premium likely to be associated with
CoreWeave’s capacity amidst the capacity ramp challenges faced by the
competitors, and the limited capacity concentration risk associated with the
company relative to competition. We maintain our Overweight rating and our
Dec-27 price target of $125.

  * Financing plan reduces reliance on capital markets, with parent-level capital needs limited to less than $5B through 2027 to deliver the existing backlog. Management laid out a funding plan that addresses the key investor concern following the recent credit selloff, indicating the company does not intend to issue parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 at current yields, and instead expects to fund the majority of remaining capex for the backlog through DDTLs matched to customer contracts, with more than 75% of 2027 committed capex tied to investment-grade and enterprise customers. The next DDTL, expected to launch in the coming weeks, is anticipated to carry a high-quality investment-grade rating with an implied yield of 7-7.5% while financing more than 90% of the associated capex, relative to a weighted average cost of debt of 7.9% at the end of 3Q (down 250bps y/y). Additionally, the company expects ~$9B of customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3B related to re-contracting existing infrastructure at premium pricing. Alongside nearly $5B of undrawn DDTL capacity, more than $9B of infrastructure already sitting in construction in progress, and additional asset-backed facilities, this leaves less than $5B of incremental parent-level capital required through 2027 to deliver the existing backlog. Management also reaffirmed that contracted cash flows from existing customer commitments are sufficient to service and repay both debt outstanding today and debt expected to be raised to deliver these contracts, including parent-level unsecured debt, before accounting for renewals.
  * Contract economics improving, with pricing momentum and re-contracting of the original fleet shortening the payback on deployed capital. Management highlighted that the newest customer contracts are among the most profitable the company has underwritten, with pricing increasing ~25% across SKUs in July, followed by a further ~10% increase later in 3Q, and continuing to move higher in 4Q, more than offsetting cost increases. Pricing for new infrastructure on 4- and 5-year contracts is moving to $20-25M per MW, while short-term capacity is being sold at ~$40M per MW annually. Importantly, the original fleet is re-contracting at premiums, with Ampere and Hopper pricing up 30-50% q/q in 3Q and above original contract pricing, producing cash flow in excess of what the company assumed when making those investments. With the asset-level debt on long-term contracts fully repaid by the end of the contract term, the more than 130K GPUs coming off contract in 2027 represent incremental annualized revenue approaching $4B at current pricing levels, rising to nearly $10B including the ~170K GPUs coming off contract in 2028, with no additional capex required. 
  * F3Q26 (Sept-end) Results: Revenue upside alongside PF operating margin reaching double digits a quarter ahead of plan. Total revenue came in at $3.66B or 168% y/y vs. JPMe of $3.53B or 159% y/y and consensus of $3.54B, with management citing favorable pricing alongside strong customer demand and execution. PF operating income tracked to $379M or 10.4% margin, well ahead of JPMe at $233M (6.6% margin) and consensus estimates of $240M (6.8% margin). Management attributed the sequential margin expansion to rising prices, growth in the short-term business, and operating leverage from continued scaling. Capex in the quarter landed above the guidance range at $14.5B or 396% of revenue vs. JPMe of $12.5B or 354% of revenue and the guidance range of $11.5-13.5B, as the company executed ahead of schedule on infrastructure delivery. In other KPIs, revenue backlog tracks to $132.5B (+138% y/y) vs. $104.2B as of 2Q, with the $28.3B sequential increase largely reflecting the ~$25B of net-new customer commitments announced in early 3Q. Active power reaches 1.7GW+ with a 200MW+ expansion in the quarter, and total contracted power grows by 900MW+ to 4.6GW+ from ~3.7GW at the end of 2Q.
  * Full-year guidance raised across revenue, profitability and exit ARR, with the capex range narrowed upward on accelerated infrastructure delivery. FY26 total revenue guidance is raised to $13.0-13.3B or 156% y/y at the midpoint (vs. $12.4-13.2B previously) compared to JPMe of $12.91B (152% y/y) and consensus of $12.82B (150% y/y), implying 4Q revenue of $4.69-4.99B or 208% y/y at the midpoint vs. JPMe of $4.72B (201% y/y) and consensus of $4.69B (198% y/y). PF operating income guidance is raised to $1,275-1,375M or 10.1% midpoint margin (vs. $960-1,150M or 8.2% midpoint margin previously), a ~200bps expansion, compared to JPMe of $1,102M (8.5% margin) and consensus of $1,060M (8.3% margin). The guide implies 4Q PF operating income of $747-847M, or ~16.5% margin at the midpoint, ahead of the low-teens 4Q margin outlined last quarter as well as JPMe of $721M (15.2% margin) and consensus of $674M (14.3% margin). FY26 exit ARR guidance is raised by $1.5B at the midpoint to $20-21B (from $18.5-19.5B prior). The FY26 capex guide is narrowed to $37-39B (from $35-39B prior) vs. JPMe of $37.05B and consensus of $36.43B. With $30.65B spent through 3Q, the guide implies 4Q capex of $6.35-8.35B vs. JPMe of $8.41B, a sharp sequential decline that reflects the pull-forward of deployments into 3Q. Active power guidance of 1.85GW+ at year-end is maintained, implying ~150MW of additions in 4Q.
  * Key notes from the callback (please reach out for more detailed notes). Management indicated that delivering only the existing backlog would still allow the company to meaningfully exceed its 2027 exit ARR floor target. The overwhelming majority of GPUs coming off contract will be re-priced at market rates, and FCF is expected to lag PF net income turning positive in FY28. Target around reaching 8GW of capacity by 2030 has not changed.

| Summary CoreWeave shares are indicated +8% post what we conclude was a solid
overall print that addressed many of the credit/funding as well as ROIC issues
that have weighed heavily on the stock over the last month. Revs (+168% to
$3.7b) and non-GAAP OMs (of 10%) in 3Q26 landed above the guide, the full year
2027 guide was inched up, the commentary about revs/MW and demand (2027
capacity is sold out) was very bullish and CoreWeave presented a financing
plan that enables them to avoid the unsecured (parent-level) debt market
entirely. We remain Buy-rated. Thoughts on the Print Apart from the headline
numbers, we’d flag: 1. On the credit side, CoreWeave is avoiding the unsecured
debt markets (considered unattractive) and is instead fully funding its growth
via asset-backed/DDTL (secured) debt, more customer pre-pays ($9bn over the
next 3 months) and a 2027 ramp in EBITDA. As a sign that the secured debt
market is indeed open, CoreWeave is planning its next DDTL deal in the coming
weeks, and on a like-for-like basis (same credit profile) this secured debt is
likely to come with a 25-75bps higher yield (tolerable). 2. CoreWeave sees “no
material risk” to its 2027 targets from capacity hurdles, with not-yet-
permitted sites in Texas equal to <2% of their 4.6 GW of contracted capacity,
with “no impact” from the recent midterms. 3. New capacity and existing
capacity rolling off contract (130,000 GPUs in 2027) is being priced at
materially higher revs/MW. But Will This Re-Rate the Stock? On all the hot-
button topics (credit access/cost, capacity hurdles, core revs and
profitability), the messaging was positive. If one were to poke any holes in
the print, it might be that a) the capacity added in 3Q26 (200 MW) was 50 MW
shy of our estimate and b) the unsecured debt markets are not attractive right
now (limiting the funding pools). Objectively though, Oracle’s Investor Day
last month also addressed similar funding, capacity and revs concerns and the
stock STILL faded. We stated in our last CoreWeave note that restoring
confidence may be a multi-quarter fix and we still believe this. We’re
encouraged by this print, but investors need more confidence in the underlying
economics of the business. Valuation: At just 2.3x revs and 3.7x adjusted
EBITDA on 2027 estimates, at the very low end of the range for the AI infra
sub-sector, with heightened investor credit concerns but no real deterioration
in the business, we remain Buy-rated. We’re maintaining our PT of $105, based
on 2.6x our CY28 sales estimates, still at the low end of the peer group.

# Flex Ltd

## Innovation Day Review: RemainCo Plays to Form as Axiom Power and FCF
Outlook is Balanced by a Subdued Cloud Forecast

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Manmohanpreet
Singh,
Marc
Vitenzon

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
FLEX, FLEX US  
Price (10 Nov 26):$76.09  
  
The Innovation Day highlighted a largely in-line outlook for Flex (RemainCo),
including a MSD organic revenue CAGR through FY29, consistent with the typical
growth profile associated with a diversified EMS asset. Importantly, the
latter is driving an operating margin outlook of 7%+ by FY29 (vs. 5.7%–5.9%
pro forma in FY27), led by revenue expansion into six high-value markets
(HVMs), including medical devices, drug delivery, energy infrastructure,
robotics, advanced networking, and satcom, which is expected to account for
35%-40% of mix by FY29 (vs. 24% in FY26), and support double-digit earnings
growth (including the use of the Axion stake for debt paydown). On the
flipside, Axiom’s outlook was particularly solid in Power, including a 40%+
revenue CAGR through CY30 on top of ~76% growth in CY27, along with EBITDA
margin tracking to high-20s in CY30 (vs. high-teens in CY26 and mid-20s in
CY27). That said, the Cloud & Cooling revenue CAGR of 10%+ surprised as it
tracked much softer than expected and well below XPU forecasts, including TPU.
While the softness is likely to be attributed to a conservative view given
expectations for growth of ~131% in CY27, the manifestation of any such upside
will likely present a headwind to the consolidated margin ramp given the lower
margin profile of Cloud & Cooling. On the positive side, FCF is now expected
to track positive in CY27, and improve further thereafter, likely easing
concerns related to the need for additional funding. Net-net, the Innovation
Day presented an outlook for Flex that tracked largely to form, while solid
expectations for Power and FCF for Axiom was balanced by a subdued (and likely
conservative) forecast for Cloud & Cooling. Importantly, all of the
aforementioned is in the backdrop of shares continuing to trade largely in
line with EMS peers on CY28E earnings despite a strong revenue growth and
materially higher, industry leading margin outlook, further justifying the
value unlock promised by the spin that remains on track for C1Q27.

    * Flex: Targeting MSD revenue growth through FY29, with margins reaching 7%+. Flex reiterated its FY27 guidance, including revenue growth of HSD–LDD (RMS growth of MSD–HSD, ITS growth of LDD to low teens) and operating margin of 5.9%–6.1% as reported (5.7%–5.9% pro forma post-spin). Directionally, Flex is targeting a MSD organic revenue CAGR from FY26 to FY29, including RMS growth of MSD–HSD and ITS growth of LSD–MSD, and operating margin tracking to 7%+ by FY29.  Interest expense is targeted to moderate by ~$100 mn relative to FY27 pro-forma as Flex exchanges its 10%–12% retained Axiom stake for debt within 24 months of the spin. Together, these drivers support double-digit EPS growth, with buybacks as further upside, alongside FCF conversion targeted at 80%+ and capex at ~2%.
    * Flex: Revenue mix from HVMs to reach 35%–40% of revenue by FY29 and drive operating margin expansion. Flex named six HVMs: medical devices, drug delivery, energy infrastructure and robotics within the RMS segment, plus advanced networking and satcom within the ITS segment. Importantly, these markets are tied to secular growth drivers, carry margins higher than the corporate average, and already have established customer positions. HVMs are expected to grow at a DD CAGR through FY29, well ahead of the corporate average, with the revenue mix expanding from 24% in FY26 to ~30% in FY27E and 35%–40% by FY29E. Flex noted two-thirds of the expansion to 7%+ margins by FY29 is driven by HVMs mix, with the rest from productivity and fixed-cost leverage.
    * Axiom: Power portfolio spans from grid-to-chip; EPC and 800V roadmap well placed for the AC-to-DC transition. Axiom’s power portfolio spans from grid to chip, covering Critical Power (switchgear, busway, PDUs and modular, with 1M+ sq ft of capacity enabling up to 50% faster deployment) and Embedded Power (sidecars, power shelves and board-level modules), which is a key differentiator given that ~half of grid-to-chip losses occur inside the rack. The EPC acquisition adds grid-forming BESS and facility power conversion, including the Agile 480 (replaces the UPS, ~92% to ~95% efficiency to the rack) and the Agile 800R (34.5 kV to 800 VDC at ~97% efficiency). Next-gen solutions include the SST-based Agile 800ST (98%+ efficiency, on the roadmap) and 800V power distribution boards (+~4 pts efficiency improvement rack-to-chip), which together lift grid-to-chip efficiency from ~80% to ~88%, worth ~$1.6–2.4 bn of annual revenue potential per GW for customers.
    * Axiom: Shift to 800V expands content per MW, adding another growth lever. Axiom’s addressable power content is ~$2.8 mn per MW today, rising to $3.4–4.0 mn per MW with the move to higher-density, 800VDC architectures ($3.4 mn in hybrid and $4.0 mn+ in future designs). This is driven by racks heading toward 600 kW and chips to 1 kW+, which require higher voltages and more advanced power distribution and conversion.
    * Axiom: Revenue to double in CY27, while EBITDA margin expands ~200–300 bps. CY27 revenue is guided to $20–21 bn, implying a growth of 105–115% y/y, driven by growth of ~76% in Power ($6.0–6.3 bn in CY27 vs. ~$3.5 bn in CY26E), along with Cloud & Cooling growth of ~131% ($14.0–14.7 bn vs. ~$6.2 bn in CY26E). Meanwhile, EBITDA margin is expected to track to 13%–14% in CY27 (vs. ~11% in CY26E), including margin in the mid-20s for Power and HSD–LDD for Cloud & Cooling. At the same time, capex intensity is expected to step down from ~10% of revenue in CY26 to ~6% in CY27, along with a transition from negative FCF to 40%+ of net income in CY27.
    * Axiom: Strong revenue and margin expansion outlook through CY30 driven by Power, while Cloud & Cooling underwhelms. Beyond CY27, revenue is guided to grow at a 20%+ CAGR to $37 bn+ by CY30, driven by growth of 40%+ in Power and 10%+ in Cloud & Cooling, while EBITDA margin is expected to reach the high teens, including high-20s for Power and LDD for Cloud & Cooling. Capex intensity is expected to further normalize to ~3–4% of revenue, with FCF conversion reaching 90%+ by CY30.

| | | Investors leaned less reserved than us into FQ1 print. While many agreed about potential headwinds to FY28 GMs, they were more optimistic about NT results, particularly as CSCO looks towards another price increase. We agree we are more cautious than checks, but post FTNT/FFIV, remain EW into print.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * We downgraded CSCO to EW last week seeing some signs of pullforward in enterprise hardware demand from FFIV / FTNT prints. 
  * Trade-off of gross margins for AI growth one that makes sense strategically, but likely limits some operating leverage, limiting upside at ~18x FY28 P/E. 
  * Investor feedback understood thesis on gross margins, but was more optimistic around FQ1 given upcoming price increase could further drive pullforward. 
  * We too think demand remains healthy, but given competitive reactions to prints where there wasn't further acceleration continues to leave us more cautious. 

  
  
Feedback post downgrade to EW. We downgraded CSCO to
EW
last week, taking chips off the table given potential demand pull-forward
signals from FTNT and FFIV prints and gross margin headwinds in out years from
a growing hyperscaler mix. These demand signals are not to weakness, just to
the idea that there has been some level of pullforward to get ahead of price
increases in 1H'CY26, meaning where we should be extrapolating growth from may
be a slightly lower point._Investors have had two push backs to the upgrade:
1) upcoming price increase and continued strong checks may cause CSCO to post
better results than other hardware peers, 2) gross margin pressure beyond what
the Street is modeling doesn't come until FY28, limiting influence on FQ1'27
print._ We tend to see 2) as the stronger argument, given margin pressure in
FY27 is largely reflected in expectations, with Street adj. GM estimates
falling ~147bps to 64.8% for FY27 and ~146bps to 65.0% for FY28 since F4Q
earnings. Given where we see more risk to is FY28 and the company is less
likely to talk about such risk in FQ1'FY27, we could be too conservative. On
1), we do think that upside due to pricing alone still likely to come with
increased scrutiny, particularly as investors look towards comps. We
understand that CSCO remains a defensive name, in an intense time of
volatility, but at ~18x FY28 P/E, we don't see enough upside to multiple to
remain OW for now.

Reiterating bogeys into F1Q27 print. See our note last week
(here)
for more details around checks. For FQ1, we expect ~$18.3-18.4B of revenue
(~23% y/y), 66% adjusted GM and $1.36-$1.38 of adjusted EPS, alongside ~18-20%
y/y growth in product orders excluding hyperscalers (~30% including
hyperscalers) and ~$3-3.5B of hyperscaler AI orders. We expect FY27 revenue
guidance to increase by ~$450M to ~$73.25B (+16% y/y) and adjusted EPS
guidance by ~$0.05-$0.07 to ~$5.14 (+18% y/y). We would expect the AI revenue
target to be raised to $8bn, from $7.5bn previously. _We have not received a
tremendous amount of pushback to our bogeys, though would say bias is likely
to the upside given the impact of pricing and higher anticipated AI orders._

broker.subject: IDEA: Infineon Technologies AG (IFXGn.DE): 2027 intact, 2028 the debate
broker.reviewed_excerpt:
| | | |   
---  
  
---  
| | |   
---  
Infineon Technologies AG (IFXGn.DE)  
2027 intact, 2028 the debate  
| | Read Full Report  
---  
(PDF: 13 Pages)  
---  
| Europe  
---  
Stock Rating   Equal-weight  
Price Target   €65.00  
Lee Simpson, Shawn Kim, Amelia M Scicluna  
November 11, 2026  
---  
| | | 2027 starts positively for Infineon, with a solid FY27 data center guide, automotive doing better than expected and signs of improving margins. That said, we remain Equal-weight, as we think outperformance will be limited amidst macro uncertainty and concerns around durability of the GW build-out.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * FY27 guide in line: sales c.€20bn (+20%+ yy), GM mid-to-high 40s% (cons c.47%), Segment margin mid-20s%. Q1 guide (sales c.€4.6bn, margin c.23%) also in line. 
  * DC sales to approach €4bn (FY26: €2.2bn), underpinned by orders in hand. Supply, not demand, is the binding constraint, so risk skewed to upside. 
  * Autos recovering with guide +mid-teens% vs our HSD-LDD% estimate, driven by the end of de-stocking, MCU/SDV ramps and China strength. 
  * H2-weighted margin bridge with lower idle costs, step-up savings, mix and pricing partly offset by start-up costs, and input costs. 
  * We keep our EW rating, PT €65. 

  
  
Welcome Reprieve. An overall positive tone, with discussion focused on
improving margins, continued AI DC momentum and even better autos sales on new
product rollouts. The capacity expansion needed to meet data center demand was
well laid out, and the sense is of a business continuing to gain in the AI
space while aiming to absorb ramp up costs at the same time. LTAs have
stretched to €10bn+ for the data center, which suggests demand visibility into
FY28 at least. Automotive is doing better than we had expected from both
channel restocking and new products. However, autos won’t transform the
business next year, as margins will still move on the strength of datacentre.
That said, things can be seen as incrementally positive in ATV. On edge
systems, project lumpiness is still holding the segment back (security and ID
solutions). All in, the headline FY27 guide is in-line, but the quality of
visibility has improved. DC is order-backed and supported by LTAs, autos are
past the de-stock, and the margin bridge should strengthen through the year as
start-up costs fade. The key upside levers are DC output (above €4bn), pricing
and FX. Into FY27 we think the key watch-points are execution on the Dresden 4
ramp and the pace of cost absorption.

Data center: backed by orders, supply constrained. The c.€4bn guide for
datacentre sales is better than we had expected, and this may yet prove
conservative. The FY split is c.€0.8bn CPU/classic and c.€3.2bn accelerators
(FY26: €1.7bn AI only; €2.2bn including classic CPU). Management stressed the
guide reflects orders in hand, not GW to be installed or share assumptions,
with some H2 customer forecasts haircut. Meanwhile, LTAs (€10bn+) underpin
visibility (2-3 year duration typical) and prepayments support capacity
buildout. The company is hopeful of GaN and vertical power delivery sales
(more so 2028 we think), whereas agentic AI is seen as lifting CPU demand, and
IFX is ramping globally across hyperscalers and GPU makers alike.

An in-line FY27 outlook. Infineon guided next year sales of c.€20bn (FY26:
€16.35bn). Power Systems (PS) is the fastest-growing segment on AI DC,
Automotive (ATV) is guided +mid-teens% and Edge Systems (ES) +low-teens%
(smart home, robotics). GM% is guided at mid-to-high 40s% (Q4: 45.1%; cons
c.47%), with the exit rate likely nearer the high 40s level, which implies
H2-weighted margin progression. Segment margin is guided at mid-20s%, from
c.23% in Q1. Finally, capex steps up to €3.0–3.5bn (Dresden 4, GaN in Villach,
SiC in Kulim), whereas adjusted FCF is guided to c.€2.2bn (c.11% of sales),
excluding c.€1bn of pre-tax proceeds from the NOR flash disposal to Winbond.
All told, a pretty in-line guide for the year ahead.

Automotive: destocking over, growth re-accelerating. The inventory correction
looks complete, and modest restocking is under way. Growth is driven by MCU
ramps on new SDV platforms, as well as by Ethernet and MOSFETs also doing
well. China grew at twice the global ATV rate in FY26, aided by exporting
Chinese OEMs prioritising supply reliability, which management claimed as a
positive for them. Notable design wins also stand out, with AURIX domain
controllers at a Japanese OEM and SiC traction inverters at a North American
EV maker. Elsewhere, high voltage drivetrain wins are re-inflecting, which is
a small surprise given this had been listing of late, but it will dilute mix
in FY27 (c.1pps headwind to group). Stepping back we see mid-teens% growth yy
as better than many had expected, although outperformance here doesn’t
necessarily drive group margins meaningfully.

Margin bridge: FY27 moving parts. We see four main moving parts when modelling
margins for FY27: (i) Reducing idle costs is a tailwind as they fall to
c.€350m (FY26: c.€600m) but remain a c.1.5pp GM drag in FY27, leaving further
operating leverage as loadings improve. (ii) Step-up in savings, mix and
pricing presents another tailwind: structural savings continue, mix improves
on AI DC, and pricing is slightly positive as 2026 power price increases
broaden across segments. However, (iii) the Dresden 4 build-out, D&A and
growing input costs are headwinds, with what we think are H1-weighted start-up
and input costs (including foundry/OSATs). Meanwhile, D&A rises to €2.2bn
(FY26: €1.9bn), with about half of the increase from the Dresden 4 build out
costs. (iv) Currency is a swing factor: the guide assumes a EUR/USD exchange
rate of $1.15, and we note that the sensitivity was changed. Now for each 1c
move, there is a c.€30m impact on quarterly sales and c.€15m on segment
result, which underlines that any USD strength is upside. As a result, we
expect margins to stay 46-47% in H1, with an improvement likely to come in H2.

We remain EW, PT €65. We continue to view Infineon as the best-positioned
analog semi for powering the data center, but see a more attractive
risk/reward elsewhere in our European semis coverage given macro uncertainty
and concerns around the durability of GW build-out. In particular, we think
risks to near-term GW installations (see
here)
may prevent Infineon from outperforming and pose a marginal risk to the
company's FY28 data centre sales. We make modest estimate revisions to reflect
updated management commentary and the new business segmentation. This leaves
our FY27/28 EPSe largely unchanged at €1.73/2.83 (prior €1.76/2.89). On
valuation, we maintain our SOTP framework to reflect the different growth
profiles of the data centre business vs the cycle segment. We see near-term
support from an improving cycle, firmer pricing and better-than-normal Q1
seasonality, but think data centre expectations remain demanding. We retain
our 30x P/E multiple for the data centre business and 18x P/E for the cycle
segment. The latter remains in the high teens, typical of a cycle recovery,
while also reflecting the multiple de-rating across global analog stocks. With
broadly unchanged EPSe, our PT remains €65. Read
